main_text.p: larminus sophisma suum exsculpit, {a}Virgilius in Aenei.li.10. simillima rei verae formam effigieque adhibet:

p.i: Tum Dea nube cava tenuem sine viribus umbram Infaciem Æneæ (visu mirabile monstrum) Dardanijs ornat telis, clypeúmque, iubásque Diuini aßimulat[?] capitis: dat inania verba, Dat sine mente sonum, gressúsque effingit euntis.

main_text.p: Vbi cava nubes, utcunque ex Bellarmini expositione sit vana & inanis, nihilo magis probat Æneæ imaginem fuisse rei minimè subsistentis formam: quàm imagines lignea in templis {b}Ethnicis & Pa-Baruc.6. 2j[?].pisticis, cavæ, quum à muribus (ut {c}simulacrum Se-Theodoret. hist.eccl. l.5.c.22.rapidis Alexandriæ) incoluntur, ostendunt eas hominum effigies non esse. Immo etiamsi notasset Bellarminus Briareum & Chimæram, non veras res, sed fictas, quas imaginatio poetica fabricavit, appellari cava imagines à Virgilio: nequaquam tamen evicisset Virgilium, aut de illis, ut fictis, loquutum esse; aut, si hoc quoque daretur, loquutum esse proprie. Nam {d}propria sunt verba, quum id significant, in quod primum denominata suntQuintilian. l.1.c.10.: unde propriam & primariam significationem conungit Bellarminus. Imago autem dicta est ab imitando, ut Bellarminus item asserit, & veram similitudinem rei proprie sonat. Quare si Virgilius hanc appellationem accommodasset rei fictæ, idq; ut fictæ: fecisset figurata significatione, vel Bellarmino judice; sive καταχρήσει[?] cum {e}Quintiliano adscribetLib.8.cap.2 & 6., sive alii cui tropo; sed figurata & secundaria significatione voce usurpasset. Ne dicâ tales quoq; fictarum rerum formas, quas imaginatio fabricat, ex aliqua verarum rerum similitudine fingi cósuevisse: sicut {f}Aristoteles docet in phantasmatis visisq; somni-De insom-niis,cap.3.

page.notes: Marginal notes printed in the right margin: a (Aeneid.li.10.), b (Baruc.6. 2j), c (Theodoret. hist.eccl. l.5.c.22.), d (Quintilian. l.1.c.10.), e (Lib.8.cap.2 & 6.), f (De insomniis, cap.3). The mark f is set in the text before "Aristoteles", at the line the note sits beside. The Greek word after "sive" is printed as a Greek word for catachresis, read uncertainly. The verse line "aßimulat" has a ligature-like glyph, read as adsimulat in the original Virgil. The reference "2j" in note b is doubtful. "Dardanijs" is printed as such. The first line starts with a fragment ("larminus"), kept as printed. The last line ends mid-word with a hyphen, continuing on the next page.
